headline: Records on lower yields. Korea falls, India hikes.
standfirst: Tuesday brought closing records for the S&P 500, up 0.58% to 7,818.93, and for the Nasdaq Composite, up 0.45% to 27,599.79, with the Dow up 0.49% to 51,521.28, its fourth straight gain. Utilities rose 3.0% and health care was the only sector lower, while the Russell 2000 fell 0.59%. The ten-year closed at 5.267%, down about 4bp from 5.31% and about 8bp below Monday's intraday high, even though the $58 billion three-year auction went at 4.932%, the highest since 2006. The August trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, the largest since March 2025, as imports hit a record on AI-related goods and oil, and euro-area retail sales rose 0.8% against 1.0% expected. Asia is lower this morning: the Kospi is down about 1.5% with LG Electronics down 9%, the Nikkei about 0.5%, and India's central bank raised its rate by 25bp to 5.5%. Brent is $101.45 on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and tanker incidents near Hormuz. Today: the ten-year auction at 13:00 ET and the Fed minutes at 14:00 ET.

bullets.title: Rates: yields eased 4bp on Tuesday, a three-year auction at the highest since 2006, and the minutes today
bullets.text: The ten-year closed at 5.267%, down about 4bp from 5.31%, and the two-year at 4.80%; the thirty-year is near 5.63%. The long Treasury ETF rose 0.22% but is down 6.0% over a month. Oil had dipped to a one-month low in WTI early on Tuesday, which helped, and Reuters called the three-year auction solid even though it went at 4.932%, the highest yield since May 2006: the bid-to-cover was 2.62 against a 2.64 ten-auction average, indirect bidders took 57.6% against a 63% average, and it cleared slightly through the when-issued yield. San Francisco's Daly said inflation may last longer than expected and that more hikes may be needed, and Kansas City's Schmid called inflation 'frustrating' and AI one of its largest drivers. October's hike is priced at about 19–20% against about 51% a week ago, with December about 85%. This morning the ten-year is back near 5.30–5.31%. Today's tests are $39 billion of ten-year notes at 13:00 ET, against 4.834% last month, and the minutes of the 16 September meeting at 14:00 ET; $22 billion of thirty-year bonds follow on Thursday.

bullets.title: Equities: records for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, led by utilities, with small caps and health care lower
bullets.text: The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,818.93 and the Nasdaq Composite at a record 27,599.79, the Dow at 51,521.28 and the Russell 2000 down 0.59% to 2,830.30; the VIX closed at 15.01. Utilities rose about 3.0%, the sector fund 2.98%, consumer discretionary 1.39% in the index and real estate 1.13%, while health care fell 0.16%. Software and services rose 1.3% to a level last seen in November 2025 on upgraded earnings forecasts, Lamb Weston rose about 12% on results and a raised outlook, and Nvidia is nearing a $6 trillion value; SpaceX is reportedly seeking $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips. Over a month technology is up 7.86% and every other sector fund is lower. Europe closed higher: the Stoxx 600 rose 0.48%, the FTSE 100 0.42%, the CAC 40 0.40% and the DAX 0.77%, with Genmab up 7.7% on a lymphoma trial. Futures this morning point to lower opens in Paris, Frankfurt and London, and US futures were little changed. Constellation Brands reports before the open and Levi Strauss after the close.

bullets.title: Data: a $105.6 billion trade deficit, weaker euro-area retail sales, and a 10.6% fall in German orders
bullets.text: The August trade deficit was $105.6 billion against $102.1 billion expected, the widest since March 2025, and July was revised to $92.8 billion from $88.6 billion. Imports rose 4.3% to a record $420.8 billion on crude oil, capital goods such as semiconductors and nonmonetary gold, and exports rose 1.4% to $315.2 billion; Capital Economics said third-quarter growth would come in well below its 4.0% forecast, closer to 2.5%, while Nationwide's Oren Klachkin read it as strong domestic demand rather than weakness. In Europe euro-area retail sales rose 0.8% year on year against 1.0% expected, with volumes up 0.1% on the month against 0.2% and fuel volumes down 1.9%, and German factory orders fell 10.6% in August, the most in seven months. The euro rebounded 0.34% on Tuesday from Monday's 16-month low as French, Italian and Greek bonds rallied after the leading candidate in next spring's presidential election outlined plans to cut spending, and it is $1.123 this morning. One estimate has the market pricing about two and a half more ECB hikes, from three and a half at the end of September, after September inflation of 3.8%.

bullets.title: Asia: Korea down 1.5%, the Nikkei lower on chip profit-taking, and India's central bank hiked to 5.5%
bullets.text: The Kospi is down 1.55% at 6,833.90 after LG Electronics fell about 9% on preliminary third-quarter profit below expectations, and the Korea ETF fell 2.64% in New York; the Taiex is down 0.32%, the Hang Seng down 0.56% with its biotech index down about 4%, and the ASX up 0.52%. The Nikkei is down about 0.5% near 70,331 after rising nearly 2,400 yen in two sessions, with Advantest, Tokyo Electron and Kioxia sold for profit, while the Topix touched a record; the yen weakened to 158.4 and Japan's real cash earnings rose 1.5% in August, an eighth straight gain. A new BoJ board member, Ayano Sato, said she favours gradual rate increases. India's central bank raised its repo rate by 25bp to 5.5%, its first hike in about three and a half years, and the rupee is 96.55 per dollar, about 2% weaker over a month; the Sensex is down 0.6%. Mainland China's markets are shut until 8 October, so the Asian read is thin.

bullets.title: Oil, gold and crypto: Brent $101 on Houthi attacks, gold near $4,150, and Bitcoin slid to about $83,800
bullets.text: December Brent is $101.45, up 0.86%, and WTI $90.09, up 0.73%. Yemen's Houthis targeted Saudi airports at Jazan and Najran and claimed an attack on a major refinery, the UK maritime agency has logged nine tanker incidents near Hormuz this month, and a storm is heading for the Gulf of Mexico; Middle East exports other than Iran's are returning toward pre-war levels and the G7 has agreed a stock release, which have capped the rise, and the EIA raised its fourth-quarter Brent forecast to about $105, $14 above its previous. Brent's 1M column still straddles the 30 September roll to December. Gold fell 0.65% to $4,160 after touching about $4,100, a two-month low, on Tuesday, with the dollar and Fed minutes in focus. All nine coins fell: Bitcoin 1.56% to $84,208, Ether 2.99% and Cardano 4.14%, and about $404 million of leveraged longs were liquidated in an hour early Wednesday as Bitcoin slid to about $83,800; Santiment noted Monday's net exchange outflow of 24,073 coins, the largest since 1 March. Brazil's Ibovespa gave back 0.52% to 205,835 after Monday's 7.7% surge, with the real near 4.98.

calendar.event: Constellation Brands before the open; Levi Strauss 17:00 ET
calendar.note: Two consumer names in a thin earnings week; the banks start on 13 October. PepsiCo reports before the open on Thursday and Delta on Friday.

The week's test of term premium: the last ten-year cleared at 4.834% and the benchmark is about 45bp higher. Tuesday's three-year went at the highest yield since 2006, with indirect bidders below average.

The record of the 12–0 hike. Daly and Schmid said more hikes may be needed; October is priced at about 19–20% and December about 85%. How many of the twelve wanted a faster path, and how the energy shock was discussed, are the questions.
The accounts of the 10 September hike land after inflation printed 3.8% and the market cut its ECB path. Claims are seen at 200,000 after 197,000.

The long bond is near 5.64%, below Monday's intraday 5.70%; the last auction cleared at 5.308%. The calendar has Waller at 04:30 ET, though a Reuters note lists him, Kashkari and Musalem for Wednesday, so check the times.
Seen 47.6 after 48.1; the one-year inflation expectations line is the one the Fed reads. Canada's jobs report is at 08:30 ET and Delta reports before the open.

calendar.event: Columbus Day: US bond market closed; Hammack 12:50 ET
calendar.note: Equities trade; Treasuries and the banks do not,
The first CPI after the September hike, previous 3.4% on the year, two weeks before 28 October, when the Fed and the Bank of Canada decide and Australia's CPI prints.

sessionNote: Wednesday opens with Asia lower and Europe called lower after records on Wall Street, which makes the day two scheduled tests rather than a headline: $39 billion of ten-year notes at 13:00 ET and the minutes at 14:00 ET. Tuesday showed the market can hold a record index alongside a ten-year near 5.27–5.31%, but it also showed a three-year auction at the highest yield in twenty years with below-average indirect demand, and Daly and Schmid both said more hikes may be needed, so the ten-year auction tail and the minutes' account of the 12–0 vote are the reads. Brent is $101 with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and tanker incidents near Hormuz offset by recovering exports; the euro holds its rebound on French bond relief while ECB pricing has been cut. Korea is the weak spot in Asia and India has hiked; mainland China is shut until 8 October.
watchOut: Reading Tuesday's yield dip as a change of direction. The ten-year fell 4bp and was back near 5.30% in Asia within hours, the three-year auction was the highest since 2006 with below-average indirect demand, and two Fed presidents said more hikes may be needed. Second, utilities: a 3% day in the most rate-sensitive sector came on a 4bp fall in the ten-year, and the sector is still down 4.5% over a month and 9.3% over three; one day does not change that. Third, the map's Brent 1M column, which still straddles the 30 September roll to December and shows a gain next to WTI's fall. Fourth, the calendar: Reuters lists Waller, Kashkari and Musalem for Wednesday while the calendar carries Waller and Musalem on Thursday, so confirm the times. Size for the 13:00 ET auction and the 14:00 ET minutes, not for the index.

archive.headline: Nasdaq record. Ten-year at a 24-year high.
archive.summary: Brazil's Ibovespa jumped 7.7% to a record after Flavio Bolsonaro led the presidential first round, the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,477.31 on Nvidia and the S&P 500 at 7,773.95. ISM services prices paid rose to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, and the ten-year touched 5.349%, its highest since 2002, before closing near 5.31%. Brent fell about 2% to $100.3 on a G7 stock release, and the euro touched a 17-month low near $1.116 on French and Spanish politics.

archive.headline: Payrolls 29,000. Yields rose anyway.
archive.summary: September payrolls rose 29,000 against about 90,000 expected with a net 60,000 downward revision, unemployment 4.2% and wages +0.1%; October's Fed hike went to about 22% priced and the Nasdaq touched a record, but the ten-year closed about 3bp higher after Logan said half a point more is needed. The G7 agreed a 100 million barrel stock release, euro-area inflation printed 3.8%, Tokyo core CPI 2.7% and the dollar index reached a 17-month high.

archive.headline: Payrolls 29,000. Yields rose anyway.
archive.summary: Weekend edition. October's Fed hike went from more than 70% priced on Monday to about 25% by Thursday on Williams, a 3.0% core PCE and Jefferson, while the long end set 2002 highs on a 2.2% GDP revision, a 58.8 Chicago PMI and ISM prices paid at 77.9; the ten-year touched 5.344% and closed 5.233%. Brent rose 4.4% on China's fuel-export halt and a third US carrier group, Nike cut its guidance, the euro hit a 16-month low on France's budget and Tokyo core CPI printed 2.7%.

archive.summary: Weekend edition. October's Fed hike went from more than 70% priced on Monday to about 25% by Thursday on Williams, a 3.0% core PCE and Jefferson, while the long end set 2002 highs on a 2.2% GDP revision, a 58.8 Chicago PMI and ISM prices paid at 77.9; the ten-year touched 5.344% and closed 5.233%. Brent rose 4.4% on China's fuel-export halt and a third US carrier group, Nike cut its guidance, the euro hit a 16-month low on France's budget and Tokyo core CPI printed 2.7%.

archive.headline: Core PCE 3.0%. Bonds' worst month since 2022.
archive.summary: Core PCE printed 3.0% against 3.3% after the BEA's annual revision rewrote July, ADP beat at 90,000, final Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% and Chicago PMI jumped to 58.8; October's hike odds slid to 35–40% while the ten-year and thirty-year rose again to close a September in which the ten-year added about 50bp, its worst month since 2022. Micron beat and guided above consensus; the November Brent contract expired at $103.53; the Nikkei rose 3.24%.

archive.headline: October hike back to a coin flip.
archive.summary: Job openings fell to a five-month low, consumer confidence to a 2014 low and Williams said there was 'no need for urgency', taking October's hike from about 70% to about 50% priced; the two-year fell 6bp while the thirty-year touched 5.621%, its highest since 2002. Brent settled 2.6% lower on recovering Saudi exports, Australia's CPI printed 4.0% and the Aussie fell through 70 cents.

archive.headline: The ten-year closed at 5.24%. Nothing else mattered.
archive.summary: The ten-year closed at 5.236%, its highest since 2007, and the S&P 500 fell 0.77% to a ten-session low as Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz offer put Brent back above $107; Cook and Barkin talked rates higher, gold fell 3% to a seven-week low, and the RBA hiked to 4.60% overnight. The November Brent roll and Washington's reply to Tehran via Qatar were the day's traps.
